initializer.name: System_InitializeRuntime
initializer.queue_command: Audio_Initialize emits command 0x0B followed by the four 24-bit pointers in low-byte-first order.

tables.name: AUDIO_Z80_PATCH_TABLE
tables.evidence: Z80 patch loader 0x1737 indexes 125 two-byte little-endian offsets; the first record is at base+0x00FA, the final record is at base+0x1219, and each selected record is copied as 0x27 bytes.

tables.name: AUDIO_Z80_CHANNEL_PARAMETER_TABLE
tables.evidence: Z80 channel setup helper 0x0E2D reads a selected two-byte offset from the pointer and copies a 0x20-byte channel-parameter record; the next startup pointer begins at 0x001BAF6F.

tables.name: AUDIO_Z80_SEQUENCE_POINTER_TABLE
tables.evidence: Z80 command 0x10 loader 0x0BDF indexes the 0x72 two-byte little-endian entries; the first header offset is 0x00E4, placing its first 0x21-byte header at 0x001BB053.

boundary_check: 0x001B9D06-0x001BAF45, 0x001BAF46-0x001BAF6E, and 0x001BAF6F-0x001BB052 are contiguous, non-overlapping ranges. The following sequence-header/stream corpus remains a separate unresolved data-extent campaign.
conclusion: The three ROM tables passed during audio startup now have explicit canonical ownership. The 68K driver image remains correctly bounded at 0x001B9D05, and no internal Z80 code/data boundaries are inferred from these table records.
